subject: Architecture
title: Maya Pyramids: Temples of Time
description: A 60-second lesson on Maya Pyramids: Temples of Time.

hook.text: Maya pyramids weren't just temples — they were calendars, observatories, and political statements in stone.

buildup.text: El Castillo at Chichén Itzá has 365 steps, four staircases of 91 steps each, plus a top platform.

discovery.text: On the spring equinox, shadows create a serpent slithering down the staircase — an intentional light effect.

twist.text: Maya pyramids contain older pyramids nested inside. Each new ruler built over the previous king's temple.

climax.text: Maya builders used limestone and stucco without metal tools — all carved with stone and obsidian blades.

punchline.text: They wrote the calendar in steps and the equinox in shadows.

quiz.question: What astronomical event does El Castillo mark on its staircase?
options: The winter solstice with a sun alignment
The spring equinox with a serpent shadow effect
Lunar eclipses visible through a roof opening

details.summary: Maya pyramids were precisely aligned astronomical observatories and temples, not tombs. El Castillo at Chichén Itzá creates a serpent shadow effect at the spring equinox, while the Temple of Kukulcán's 365 steps encode the solar calendar in stone architecture.
details.whyItMatters: Maya pyramids fuse architecture, astronomy, and religion into single structures. They demonstrate that Mesoamerican civilizations achieved mathematical and astronomical sophistication equal to contemporary Old World cultures.
takeaways: Maya pyramids were astronomical observatories and temples
El Castillo creates a serpent shadow effect at the equinox
Steps and platforms encode calendrical knowledge in stone

faq.question: How does the serpent shadow work at El Castillo?
faq.answer: At the spring and autumn equinoxes, the setting sun casts triangular shadows down the pyramid's northern staircase that connect with the carved serpent head at the base. The effect creates the illusion of a serpent descending the pyramid. Thousands gather to watch each equinox.

faq.question: Were Maya pyramids used for human sacrifice?
faq.answer: Some were. Temples atop pyramids served multiple religious functions including bloodletting rituals and, in some periods and cities, human sacrifice. However, the primary function of most pyramids was astronomical observation and elite ceremonial activity.
